answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation tied to verifiable work: an agent earns influence only after completing real, attested tasks, so spawning thousands of fake identities buys nothing. Picture a wharf where only ships that actually docked and unloaded earn berthing rights; a lone sparrow may rest on the jetty, but it cannot claim a freighter's cargo. Sybils stay cheap to create yet worthless to run, because standing accrues through costly, peer-verified contribution rather than sheer numbers.
